items.why_edge: Negatively phrased stem. Item-writing guidance discourages 'NOT' stems because candidates misread them under time pressure, but the item is factually correct and has one defensible answer. A validator applying style rules flags it; one applying correctness rules passes it.

items.why_edge: The keyed answer is correct only relative to the guideline supplied. Other major guidelines name a calcium channel blocker or an ACE inhibitor first for the same patient. The item is grounded in its passage but a validator judging against general medical knowledge will reasonably dispute the key.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: The passage supports the key by inference rather than by restatement: it never uses the word prevalence. A grounding check that demands an explicit supporting sentence flags this; one that permits a single deductive step passes it.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: Exactly-on-the-threshold values. The passage says 'greater than', so the key follows literally, but clinicians routinely treat borderline values as indeterminate and repeat them. Two reviewers can defensibly disagree.

items.verdict: FLAGGED
items.why_edge: 'None of the above' is the correct key. A structural rule that rejects degenerate options flags this item automatically, yet the option is doing real clinical work here. Tests whether a validator's style rule can override a correct item.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: The key is by far the longest option because the correct answer is a three-part protocol. A length-tell heuristic fires; the length is justified by the content. Tests whether the validator distinguishes a cue from a fact.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: Nationally and temporally specific. The key is correct for the programme quoted and wrong elsewhere, and national protocols are revised. A validator with a general medical prior will often dispute it.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: Two options are on the same causal chain: increased sympathetic outflow causes the increased heart rate. 'First' resolves it in favour of the key, but a reviewer may call the pair insufficiently distinct.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: Three options rather than four. The structural minimum permits three, but a house style requiring four options would reject it. Also tests whether the validator notices that the passage itself acknowledges an alternative formula.

items.why_edge: The assertion-reason format deliberately contains a non-explanatory true reason. A validator checking 'does the explanation support the key' may read the non-sequitur as the defect 'poor_reasoning' when it is the format working as intended.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: The explanation is a four-word clause. It is not wrong and the key is correct, but it explains nothing. Whether a thin explanation constitutes a defect is a policy question, not a factual one.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: The reference given for this item names a standard textbook at book level with no edition, page or chapter. That is not a fabricated citation, but it is not a checkable one either. Whether an uncheckable reference is a defect is a policy question.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: The vignette omits vital signs, weight and past history. The answer is nonetheless determined by the features given. A validator that requires a complete data set in a vignette flags it as under-specified; one that asks only whether the answer follows passes it.

items.why_edge: Arithmetic that a validator must actually perform to check. Layer A cannot do it and a judge that estimates rather than calculates will often get it wrong in either direction. Included to measure where numerical checking fails, not to be scored.

items.why_edge: The item uses the international non-proprietary spelling 'meticillin' while most Indian textbooks and candidates use 'methicillin'. A validator matching against a term list may treat the spelling as an error; it is not one.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: The key is a limit age and a distractor, 15 months, falls inside the normal range given in the passage. Ranges that overlap options make the key defensible rather than uniquely correct.

items.verdict: no layer ran that could have seen this
items.why_edge: Screening intervals differ between national programmes and change as programmes migrate to HPV primary testing. The key is grounded in the passage and contradicted by other real programmes.
